headline: Sleep isn't passive—it's when your brain cleans house, consolidates memories, and repairs your body
universal_truth: Rest is productive; doing nothing is sometimes doing everything
fun_facts: During sleep, your brain flushes out toxic waste products through the glymphatic system
The record for longest time without sleep is 11 days—the person experienced hallucinations and cognitive decline
Every animal with a nervous system sleeps, even if just for brief periods
discussion_questions: Why do we spend a third of our lives unconscious?
What happens when you don't get enough sleep?
How does sleep affect your thinking and emotions?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: You spend about 26 years of your life asleep. That seems like wasted time—but sleep isn't nothing. It's when your brain consolidates memories, flushes toxins, and repairs damage. Sleep isn't passive; it's essential maintenance.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: We know sleep is necessary—miss enough and you die. But what actually happens during those hours of unconsciousness that's so important?

options.text: The brain consolidates memories, clears metabolic waste, repairs tissues, and regulates hormones—it's active maintenance, not shutdown
options.response: Yes. Sleep is a highly active state—different from waking but just as busy. Your brain is working hard on tasks it can only do when you're not conscious.

options.text: The body rests and conserves energy for the next day
options.response: Energy conservation is part of it, but much more happens during sleep...

q1.title: Memory Consolidation
q1.script: While you sleep, your brain replays the day's experiences, moving important information from short-term to long-term memory. Students who sleep after studying remember more than those who stay awake. Sleep is learning's partner.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Memory Consolidation"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Brain Cleaning
q2.script: Your brain produces toxic waste products during the day. During sleep, the glymphatic system—a cleanup crew—flushes these toxins away. Without this nightly cleaning, waste accumulates. Chronic sleep deprivation links to dementia.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Body Repair
q3.script: Growth hormone releases primarily during sleep—why children need more. Muscles repair, immune systems strengthen, wounds heal faster. Athletes who sleep more perform better and recover quicker. Sleep is physical reconstruction.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Rest is productive. Sleep teaches that doing nothing is sometimes doing everything—the work just happens invisibly. Prioritize sleep; it's not laziness, it's maintenance.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 131. Tomorrow, we'll explore why we dream. Until then, consider whether you're giving your brain enough time to do its nightly maintenance.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Sleep Audit - Evaluate Your Rest
growTrack.activity: Track your sleep for a week—hours, quality, how you feel. Are you getting enough? Sleep deprivation accumulates silently. Notice the connection between sleep and your thinking, mood, and energy. Adjust accordingly.
